summary: Uses Digital and IT’s mature-team estimate as the high-water mobilisation ceiling while distinguishing the four-post permanent product core from specialist/service capacity whose enduring sourcing and Student Hub attribution remain to be validated.
detailSummary:
The Digital and IT high-water model remains the prudent ceiling for mobilisation staffing, but the enduring workforce story is now made explicit. The current planning assumption is a 4.0 FTE permanent Digital and IT product core from the outset: Product Manager, Backend Engineer, Full-Stack Developer and UX/UI Designer. At the current Digital and IT cost rates these posts have a combined full-year run-rate of approximately £323,856. Mobilisation funding carries them through June 2029 and recurrent Digital and IT establishment takes over from July 2029, with the Product Manager’s eventual Student-versus-Staff Hub allocation still to be settled.

The remaining currently costed mature-team capacity totals up to approximately £277,224 per full year: Solution Architect / Technical Lead, Infuse QA, fractional Azure DevOps, Dynamics Developer, fractional Cloud Infrastructure and fractional IAM. These lines remain in the high-water funding ceiling until Digital and IT confirms which are dedicated, shared, existing, externally sourced or attributable to another programme. They are therefore visible BAU risk, but not assumed permanent Student Hub posts. Product Owner remains Mark Peace from existing workload and the IT Delivery Manager remains an existing-capacity assumption.

The Hub operating-cost model now sits explicitly with 4.1.2. Paid student visioning and co-design is treated as an annual £15,000 product capability across mobilisation and BAU. Azure, environments and platform costs ramp £50,000 / £75,000 / £100,000 across the three mobilisation years and retain a £100,000 BAU high-water allowance. A separate student-facing AI inference, retrieval and token-consumption planning allowance is introduced at £50,000 / £75,000 / £100,000, also retaining £100,000 as a BAU high-water allowance. This runtime AI budget is distinct from the £90,000 annual Devin/Cognition engineering-productivity allowance in 4.1.3 and must be validated with Jon Ward and James Costerton using an explicit demand and unit-economics model.

On this revised high-water basis, the current Digital Student Experience Hub profile is approximately £638,720 in 2026/27, £924,080 in 2027/28 and £974,080 in 2028/29: £2,536,880 across mobilisation. This remains within the £3.0m strategic envelope and leaves £463,120 unallocated headroom. The current worst-case recurrent exposure is approximately £906,080 per year before the enduring 4.1.1 knowledge/content operating model: £601,080 mature-team staffing and specialist capacity, £90,000 agentic development, £100,000 Azure/platform, £100,000 student-facing AI consumption and £15,000 recurring paid student co-design. That £906,080 remains a risk ceiling, not a settled BAU budget; the permanent-post component currently identified within it is £323,856 per year, while £277,224 of mature-team specialist/service capacity is deliberately still open to reduction or alternative sourcing.

operatingCostModel.title: Enduring product workforce commitments
operatingCostModel.summary: Separate the permanent Digital and IT product core from the remaining high-water specialist and service capacity so the recurrent liability has a clear workforce meaning.

newInvestment.item: BAU permanent four-post Digital and IT product core
newInvestment.estimatedCost: £323,856 annual constant-price run-rate from July 2029 for the Product Manager (£95,568), Backend Engineer (£81,024), Full-Stack Developer (£81,024) and UX/UI Designer (£66,240). Product Manager cost allocation with the Staff Digital Hub remains to be settled.
